hypotheses.statement: solang performs compile-time constant overflow detection and rejects expressions like type(uint256).max + 1 with a hard error, while solc accepts them and relies on the runtime Panic(0x11) checked-arithmetic revert. This means probes mixing runtime-overflow tests with other revert-reason checks will produce COMPILE_ASYMMETRY false positives unless overflow is triggered with non-constant operands.

evidence.note: solang rejected the source at compile time: 'value ...936 does not fit into type uint256' at 'return m + 1;' where m = type(uint256).max. solc compiled fine. Runtime revert-reason comparison never executed.

hypotheses.next_probe: Rewrite the overflow step as function overflow(uint256 m) external pure returns (uint256) { return m + 1; } called with type(uint256).max as an argument (runtime value, not constant) and compile under both toolchains; prediction: both compile, and both revert at runtime — then compare the decoded panic payloads (0x11 arithmetic overflow) between solc and solang.
